newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index ends sharply down on HK tumble.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends sharply down on HK tumble.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index took a heavy blow on Tuesday, responding to a slide in the market in neighbouring Hong Kong, to close with heavy losses, brokers said.

The hard currency B index dived 11.84 points or 7.46 percent to 146.88, while turnover shrank to HK$310 million from last Friday's HK$700 million. Shenzhen's B share market was closed for a day on Monday for holiday.
"Shenzhen's B index was easily hurt by Hong Kong's tumble because last week's B index surge was built on Hong Kong's market optimism," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.

The B index performed unusually strongly toward the end of last week, closing at a 10 percent limit-up on Thursday as funds were attracted by lower prices after a buying rush in H shares, or mainland shares listed in Hong Kong.
"The recent B share gains were not built on fundamentals, so investors dash away when things turn slightly for the worse," an analyst at Sun Hung Kai Investment Services in Shenzhen said.
On Tuesday, the H shares became a victim of broad market selling triggered by fears of a speculative attack on the Hong Kong dollar and a surge in interbank rates.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index, or H-share index, was down 6.60 percent by mid-afternoon.
The B index also fell on profit-taking. Investors returning from a three-day break kicked off the morning by cashing in their recent prizes, analysts said.

"On this count, I don't think the index will fall much further," an analyst at J&A Securities said. "When profit-taking has washed out some gains, many investors will soon take positions in the comparatively cheap B share market."
Analysts said the index was likely to remain volatile in the near term, with much attention focusing on the majority of listed companies that have yet to release 1997 interim results.
Analysts following the debut of Luthai Textile Joint Stock Co Ltd had a mixed response.
Although the stock defied market weakness and closed at HK$2.37 against the offer price of HK$1.93, analysts had said earlier that they expected it to trade at above HK$3.0.
"This shows the market has not got back on its feet since the government crackdown," said an analyst at a major foreign brokerage, referring to measures since May to cool the overheated markets.
Shenzhen North Jianshe Motorcycle Co Ltd fell to its 10 percent limit-down level of HK$2.48 after reporting a 51 percent year-on-year decrease in first half net profits.
Leading pesticide maker Hubei Sanonda Co Ltd fell sharply despite posting a 44 percent year-on-year rise in its interim net profits. It closed down HK$0.50 to HK$4.53.

The A share market was quieter. It edged up 0.04 points or 0.01 percent to 365.51, following the Shenzhen Development Bank's announcement to honour its original dividend plan. It had earlier been punished for trading its own stocks.
The bank's shares rose 0.90 yuan to 31.41 yuan.
